Section: section_1 — From ODEs to PDEs: A Visual Shift

Lecture lines:
ODEs describe motion along a single path.
[Asset: animation_1_ode_point]
PDEs capture change across multiple dimensions.
[Asset: animation_2_pde_ripple]
Think of ripples on a pond surface.

Planned animations:
Fade in title "From ODEs to PDEs" in #FFFFFF.
Display single particle moving on a line (ODE).
Transform line into a 2D mesh grid.
Animate heat diffusing across the grid.
Highlight the transition from ODE to PDE.

Section: section_2 — Defining the Operators

Lecture lines:
Partial derivatives isolate change by direction.
[Asset: animation_1_partial_derivative]
We analyze slopes North and East separately.
[Asset: animation_2_hiker_slope]
This isolates directional rate of change.

Planned animations:
Display operator notation: L(u) = f in #FFD700.
Show differentiation operator as a dynamic movement.
Animate the linearity property: L(au+bv) = aL(u)+bL(v).
Highlight the divergence operator in vector field context.
Show Laplacian operator as a 2D curvature measure.

Section: section_3 — The Heat Equation: A Core PDE

Lecture lines:
Heat equations model temperature flow over time.
[Asset: animation_1_heat_eq]
Change equals spatial curvature of temperature.
[Asset: animation_2_curvature_viz]
Heat naturally smooths out over time.

Planned animations:
Write u_t = α ∇²u in #00FFFF.
Represent u(x,t) as a surface on a grid.
Simulate heat smoothing out over time.

Section: section_4 — Boundary and Initial Conditions

Lecture lines:
Constraints ensure unique PDE solutions.
[Asset: animation_1_boundary_conditions]
Initial conditions set state at time zero.
[Asset: animation_2_initial_state]
Boundaries fix edges, like a guitar string.

Planned animations:
Show Dirichlet condition: u = 0 on boundary.
Show Neumann condition: du/dn = 0 on boundary.
Animate initial condition u(x,0) as a starting pulse.

Section: section_5 — Applications and Summary

Lecture lines:
PDEs model complex real-world phenomena.
[Asset: animation_1_fluid_dynamics]
From weather patterns to financial markets.
[Asset: animation_2_weather_map]
Modeling, constraints, and solving define PDEs.

Planned animations:
Show temperature distribution across a metal plate.
Highlight real-world diffusion in chemical processes.
Summarize ODE vs PDE path using a checklist.

        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
